name: Imjin Border Hills
inspired_by: The western sector of the Korean Demilitarized Zone as of 2026: forested granite hills and rice-paddy valleys along a large river, the 4 km wide DMZ with its fences and guard posts, a river estuary on the west, South Korean border towns and military bases to the south, and North Korean fortified hills to the north. The DPRK declared the ROK a 'hostile state' in 2024 and has fortified its side further. All towns are fictional.
climate: Humid continental with monsoon (Koppen Dwa). Hot humid summers (28-32 C) with the monsoon rains (changma) in July-August; cold dry winters (-5 to -15 C) with Siberian winds and frozen rivers; 1,200-1,400 mm rain, 60% in summer.
seasons: Winter (Dec-Feb): very cold, dry, snow patches, frozen paddies and river edges, clear skies
Spring (Mar-May): yellow dust from the continent, azaleas on hills, rice planting
Monsoon summer (Jun-Aug): heavy rain, river floods, humid heat, dense green cover
Autumn (Sep-Nov): clear and crisp, rice harvest, red maples, migratory cranes in the DMZ

vegetation: rice paddies (flooded in summer, stubble in winter)
ginseng fields under black shade cloth
dense regrown scrub and forest on former fields
reed and wetland in old paddies
grasslands burned for visibility near fences

terrain.relief: Steep granite hills (200-650 m) with sharp ridgelines and narrow valleys of flat rice paddies at 10-50 m, a large meandering river with high bluffs crossing the map west to the estuary.
features: steep forested ridges with rock outcrops
a large river with basalt cliffs and sandbars
the 4 km DMZ band with the Military Demarcation Line in its centre
southern limit fence (triple fence with cameras), guard posts (GP) on hilltops
infiltration tunnels (level geometry) under the DMZ
anti-tank walls and dragon's teeth on valley roads
terrain.water: One large river with a tributary, an estuary on the west edge (neutral-zone waters), reservoirs, paddy irrigation channels; the river freezes partially in winter.

generator.approach: Heightmap at 10 m. Ridged multifractal hills with steep sides, valleys flattened to paddy terraces (quantised 0.5-1 m steps) where slope is low; river carved as a deep meandering spline with bluffs; estuary as tidal flats on the west edge. The DMZ band (4 km wide, east-west) is a mask: vegetation regrowth and minefield hazard tags inside, fences on its edges.
generator.erosion: Hydraulic erosion (60 iterations) for steep gullies; thermal cap 45 degrees with rock faces.
generator.rivers: Main river spline west to the estuary with bluffs; tributaries by flow accumulation; reservoirs at valley dams.
generator.settlement_flattening: Villages at valley edges at the foot of hills; towns on river terraces; bases on flattened hill shoulders.
generator.notes: Movement funnels into valley roads guarded by anti-tank walls; ridges give observation. The DMZ band is mined and only GPs and patrol paths are safe (hazard rule). Tunnels are level geometry for set-piece contracts.

settlements.architecture: South Korean border town: four- to six-storey concrete buildings with neon signs on every floor (restaurants, academies, PC rooms), 15-25 storey apartment blocks with numbered facades, a traditional market, churches with red neon crosses, military uniform shops near bases.
layout_rules: commercial core along the main road and station
base gates on the edge with shops

settlements.architecture: Farming villages: single-storey houses with blue, green or red tiled or metal roofs, some traditional hanok with curved tile roofs, vinyl greenhouses, storage sheds, a village hall and a pavilion; 'civilian control line' villages with military checkpoints.
settlements.wall_class: Block and brick medium; hanok timber and mud walls thin; greenhouses none.
layout_rules: at the foot of a hill facing south over paddies
village hall and a big zelkova tree

settlements.architecture: Military sites: South Korean and US bases (barracks, motor pools, hangars), DMZ guard posts (GP) as small concrete forts on hilltops, observation posts with viewing decks, the southern-limit triple fence with cameras and patrol paths, North Korean GPs and bunkers on the opposite hills, anti-tank wall structures on roads, the joint-security-type truce village with blue huts (neutral).
settlements.wall_class: GPs and bunkers thick; huts thin.
layout_rules: GPs on hilltops inside the DMZ every 1-2 km
bases 5-15 km south of the line
anti-tank walls on every valley road

settlements.architecture: Farm compounds in the civilian-control zone: a house, a cattle shed, greenhouses; farmers need passes to enter.
layout_rules: isolated in paddy valleys near the line

infrastructure.roads: A freeway and a national road running toward the line (ending at checkpoints), valley roads with anti-tank walls, military patrol roads along fences, a road and rail bridge over the river (one ends at the DMZ).
infrastructure.rail: A line ending at a border station near the DMZ (unused cross-border link).
infrastructure.power: Power lines, a substation; DPRK side dark at night.
infrastructure.ports: None for shipping (the estuary is a neutral zone); small fishing harbours south of the estuary; LHD offshore of the estuary mouth.
infrastructure.airfields: Army aviation base with helicopters (AI), helipads at bases.
infrastructure.checkpoints: Civilian control line checkpoints, bridge checkpoints, the DMZ fence gates; DPRK side unseen except GPs.

pois.description: South Korean GP on a hilltop inside the DMZ: concrete fort with firing ports, towers, a helipad and a single fenced road through minefields.
pois.contract_use: counter-infiltration sweep from a GP (client kor)

pois.description: Discovered infiltration tunnel under the DMZ: an intercept shaft, a narrow rock tunnel with rails, water and a concrete plug (level geometry).
Triple fence with razor wire, cameras, sensors, lights and a patrol path; breach marks found.
pois.contract_use: counter-infiltration sweep after a breach (client kor)

pois.description: OP with a viewing deck, telescopes and bunkers overlooking the DPRK propaganda village and GPs.
pois.contract_use: reconnaissance; VIP protection on a visit (clients kor, usa)

pois.description: Neutral joint-security-type area with blue conference huts on the line and buildings on both sides; ceremonial guards.
pois.contract_use: VIP protection during talks (client kor, high sensitivity)

pois.description: Road and rail bridge over the river with checkpoints, anti-tank structures and a bunker.
pois.contract_use: hold the bridge in escalation; convoy chokepoint

pois.description: Crashed DPRK reconnaissance drone in a paddy field near a village; police and army cordon.
Islet in the estuary with a marine post, tidal flats and a lighthouse; neutral-zone waters around.
Combined base with motor pools, barracks, hangars and a helipad.
pois.contract_use: contract board; noncombatant evacuation assembly (clients usa, aus, nzl)

pois.description: Unused border railway station with a big terminal hall and a car park, near the DMZ.
pois.contract_use: noncombatant evacuation assembly point; hold in escalation

pois.description: Field where trash balloons from the north came down; debris and a sensor package.
pois.contract_use: secure site and recover debris (client kor)

pois.description: North Korean guard post on a facing hill: concrete fort, loudspeakers, trenches. Escalation objective only.

weather.visibility_notes: River and valley fog at dawn; monsoon rain grounds helicopters; dense summer foliage limits sight to metres; clear winters give long views.
weather.dust_or_snow: Yellow dust in spring; light snow in winter.

civilians.behaviour: Busy border towns with soldiers on leave; farmers in civilian-control-line villages work only in daylight with passes; tourists at observation posts. Civil-defence drills send people to shelters. North of the line, no civilians are encountered on the map.
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: Towns are dense; the DMZ and DPRK sector have no civilians; civilian-control villages are small and sensitive.

factions_present.where: South of the line: GPs, fences, OPs, bases, bridges; marines at the estuary.
Combined base and aviation; truce village staff.
North of the line: GPs and bunkers on facing hills, artillery positions in hillsides, infiltration teams, drones and balloons.
UN Command staff and liaison officers at the truce village and combined base.
UN Command staff at the truce village.
Evacuation planning team for Japanese nationals (plausibility: no Japanese forces in Korea; liaison only).
No forces on the DMZ; appears only in escalation intel and as an off-map factor beyond the north edge (plausibility flagged).

frontline: An armed truce. The line does not move in the default state; prk provocation events (drones, balloons, fence incidents, GP fire, infiltration teams) raise alert and post counter-infiltration, recovery and site-security contracts. A late-game escalation scenario (proposed) sees artillery and assaults across the DMZ toward the bridges, with valley roads and anti-tank walls as the defence.
contract_hooks: Counter-infiltration sweep after a fence breach (client kor)
Recover a downed drone from a paddy (client kor)
Reconnaissance from an OP or estuary islet (clients kor, usa)
Noncombatant evacuation assembly at the combined base or border station (clients usa, aus, nzl, jpn)
VIP protection at the truce village during talks (client kor)
Secure a balloon landing site (client kor)
Escalation scenario: hold the river bridge (late game)

hot_zones.name: DMZ escalation (late game, fictional what-if)
hot_zones.layout: prk HQ in a hillside bunker complex north of the line; 5 GPs and artillery sites as outposts; checkpoints at valley mouths; infiltration and drone teams; 2 QRF groups; the river bridge as the friendly anchor

insertion.fob: LHD offshore of the estuary mouth (outside the neutral zone, proposed); inland FOB at the combined base. Roads through checkpoints; helicopters in good weather; AAVs on the estuary and river.

early_game_notes: Peer-state theatre (prk late tier); late campaign.
ambient_audio: cranes and geese in the DMZ
